title: Enterprise Onboarding & Operational Playbook - Onboarding, Escalation, Integration, Health Checks, and QBRs
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended process for enterprise customer onboarding, technical integration checkpoints, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, and recurring health checks / QBR materials. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and SRE teams to ensure predictable, SLA-backed onboarding and ongoing operational excellence for enterprise customers.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: CS managers, Solutions Engineers, Technical Support, SREs, and Customer Engineering.
- Scope: New enterprise customers (Dedicated, Private, or Hosted API with enterprise contract). Includes pre-sales handoff, 0-90 day onboarding, integration validation, incident/escalation steps, recurring health checks, and QBR agenda/templates.

1) Goals and success criteria
- Time-to-first-production: target <= 30 days from contract signature for standard integrations (exceptions documented per account).
- Integration validation: API keys, routing, auth, and data residency validated in first 10 business days.
- Operational baseline: customer has dashboards in Redwood Console and alerting configured before go-live.
- SLA adherence: support acknowledgement targets met (see Support SLA table).

2) Onboarding owner and roles
- Customer Success (owner): overall program manager for the account.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): leads technical integration, sample prompts, latency/cost tuning, model selection.
- Support (tiered): handles operational issues post-onboarding. Level 2 (L2) Support and SRE collaborate for infrastructure incidents.
- Customer Technical Contact: customer-appointed technical owner.

3) Onboarding checklist (0-90 days)
Table: Checklist, Owner, Target date, Status
- Step 1 - Contract & onboarding kickoff call (CS): Day 0-2 - Confirm legal, security forms, community ACLs, and initial stakeholders.
- Step 2 - Access provisioning (CS/SE): Day 1-3 - Create org in Redwood Console, provision API keys, and configure role-based access (RBAC).
- Step 3 - Network & security review (SE/Security): Day 1-7 - Exchange IP allowlists, VPN/VPC info, and KMS/HSM key configurations for Private deployments.
- Step 4 - Test integration & smoke tests (SE): Day 3-14 - Run sample generation, streaming, embeddings, and API edge cases.
- Step 5 - Performance & cost tuning (SE/CS): Day 10-30 - Apply batching, cache, and quantization recommendations; produce cost forecast.
- Step 6 - Observability & alerts (CS/SRE): Day 10-30 - Provide Redwood Console dashboards, define SLOs and alert thresholds, and set up Slack/PagerDuty routing.
- Step 7 - Operational readiness & runbook handoff (CS/SRE): Day 20-45 - Deliver support runbook, escalation contact list, and post-go-live monitoring plan.
- Step 8 - Go-live & smoke verification (CS/SE/SRE): Day 30-60 - Validate production traffic, error rates, and cost vs. forecast.
- Step 9 - QBR and optimization plan (CS/SE): Day 60-90 - Present metrics, model regressions, and next-step recommendations.

4) Support SLA and response targets
- P1 (production outage / customer-facing downtime affecting >50% of requests): Initial acknowledgement <= 1 hour (24/7), mitigation updates every 30 minutes, target mitigation <= 4 hours for known-class incidents.
- P2 (partial outage / degraded performance): Initial acknowledgement <= 4 business hours, updates every 2 hours, target mitigation <= 24 hours.
- P3 (functional but impaired / non-critical): Initial acknowledgement <= 1 business day, target mitigation <= 5 business days.
- P4 (general question / feature request): Acknowledgement <= 3 business days.
Notes: Internal PagerDuty service: RDW-Enterprise-Support. Slack channels: #enterprise-support (public), #oncall-sre (ops-only). For Private deployments, CS must confirm the customer's on-call routing and PagerDuty integration during the network & security review.

5) Escalation playbook (technical incidents)
- Step 0 - Triage (Support L1): Confirm customer, collect logs, reproduce issue if possible, gather request IDs, timestamps, and model/version. Use support intake template.
- Step 1 - L2 / SE involvement: If not resolvable in 1 hour for P1 or 4 hours for P2, escalate to L2 and SE. Attach collected artifacts and run basic perf/profile checks with the runtime.
- Step 2 - SRE and infra escalations: If the incident appears infrastructure-related (capacity, kernel OOM, GPU failures), escalate to SRE and reference PagerDuty service RDW-Infra.
- Step 3 - Engineering / releases: For suspected regressions tied to model or runtime releases, open an internal incident in Jira with label "enterprise-incident" and CC product/serving-runtime owners.
- Step 4 - Customer updates and RCA: Provide customer-facing updates per SLA cadence. After mitigation, schedule a post-incident review within 5 business days and share a written RCA (owner: SRE + SE).
Contact list (primary escalation contacts):
- Support L2: support-l2@redwood-inference.com (monitor via RDW-Enterprise-Support PD)
- SE escalation: se-enterprise@redwood-inference.com
- SRE on-call: see PagerDuty schedule (link in Redwood Console)
- Executive escalation (only for high-severity multi-customer incidents): ops-leads@redwood-inference.com

6) Support intake template (required on first report)
Please collect and include:
1) Customer org ID and environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
2) API key or request ID(s) (redact full keys in public comms)
3) Timestamps (UTC) and example payloads
4) Model name + version + quantization profile (if any)
5) Error messages, stack traces, and Redwood Console correlation IDs
6) Traffic rate and any recent configuration changes

7) Integration guide - technical checkpoints (SE checklist)
- Auth: Verify API key creation and RBAC. Example curl to validate API key:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
- Endpoints: Confirm required endpoints are reachable from customer network (list: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings).
- Streaming: Validate chunked streaming in customer environment (sample SDK tests in repo github.com/redwood-inference/enterprise-sdks).
- Webhooks & callbacks: Confirm endpoints accept POSTs and validate TLS ciphers (TLS 1.2+ recommended).
- Rate limits & quotas: For Dedicated customers, verify per-route rate limits and burst policies match contract.
- Observability: Ensure customer can access the following dashboards: per-route latency, token cost, error rate, and model version distribution. Share pre-built dashboard template (attach as JSON in onboarding artifact).

8) Known issues and workarounds (operational, curated)
- ISSUE 2025-RT-01: Intermittent 5xx errors during high-concurrency generation on older 32GB instances.
  Workaround: Route high-concurrency requests to dedicated pools with continuous batching enabled; temporarily lower max_concurrency to 8 per worker. SE owner: Marco Ruiz.
- ISSUE 2025-SEC-02: Private deployment KMS rotation failure during upgrade window.
  Workaround: Schedule KMS rotation after upgrade completion and verify key alias mapping; use offline key-import process for air-gapped customers. SE + Security escalation required.
- ISSUE 2026-API-03: Client SDK retries result in duplicate function calls for function-calling tools.
  Workaround: Add idempotency tokens in client payloads; use the SDK helper "safe_call" wrapper. Engineering owner: Priya Singh.
Notes: Each known issue entry must include reproducible steps, owner, severity, and recommended mitigation. Maintain the Known Issues index under this directory and tag entries by year and subsystem.

9) Observability and health checks (pre-go-live and recurring)
Pre-go-live validations (must pass before production traffic):
- Connectivity: all endpoints reachable from customer network with <100ms RTT (where regionally practical).
- Latency P95: generation P95 < 200ms for target workload in test harness.
- Error rate: backend 5xx < 0.5% during sustained load test (5-10 minutes).
- Cost forecast: projected token cost within +/- 20% of estimate for expected volume.
Recurring health checks (weekly/monthly):
- Weekly: token consumption by endpoint, error spikes, new model-version rollouts, top-10 slowest prompts.
- Monthly: 95/99th percentile latency trends, total monthly token spend vs forecast, SLO breaches and incident summaries.
Dashboards and queries (examples):
- Redwood Console > Dashboards > Account > Per-route latency (P50/P95/P99), Token cost by route, Error rate by model.
- Alerting: create alerts for P95 latency > 2x baseline, error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes, and sudden >30% increase in token spend vs 24h moving average.

10) Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template and agenda
Recommended attendees: CS lead, Customer Technical Lead, SE, SRE (as needed), Product (optional).
Agenda:
1) Executive summary (5 minutes): Adoption, highlights, and risks.
2) Operational review (15 minutes): Uptime, incidents since last QBR, SLOs and any breaches.
3) Usage & economics (15 minutes): Token spend, per-route cost, forecast vs actual, and suggestions from Redwood Optimize.
4) Model & quality review (15 minutes): Model versions in use, recent regressions, prompt improvements, and evaluation results.
5) Roadmap & next steps (10 minutes): Upcoming features, dedicated capacity plans, and timeline for any migration.
6) Action items and owners (5 minutes): Clear owners, milestones, and due dates.
Deliverables to attach to QBR:
- Dashboard export (last 90 days)
- Top 10 prompts and quality metrics (precision/recall where applicable)
- Cost optimization plan (batching, cache, model quantization suggestions)
- Post-QBR action tracker in Jira (label: qbr-<customer-org>)

11) Operational runbooks and artifacts to deliver on handoff
- Onboarding artifact bundle (zip) containing: API key details (redacted in customer copy), runbooks, dashboard templates, smoke test scripts, test dataset and prompts, and support intake template.
- Runbooks: "how to collect request traces", "how to rotate API keys", "how to add RBAC roles" (each with step-by-step commands and expected outputs).
- Post-go-live patrol checklist: daily logs review, error spike triage, and weekly cost review.

12) Continuous improvement and feedback loop
- Post-onboarding survey (CS to run at Day 30): collect feedback on technical experience, docs, and SE interactions.
- Quarterly product feedback: collate recurring asks and tag in product board under "enterprise-requests".
- Regression monitoring: set up evaluation prompt sets for each customer where output quality matters; trigger alerts on quality regression.

Appendices
A. Useful links and templates:
- Support intake template (link to artifact in onboarding bundle)
- PagerDuty service: RDW-Enterprise-Support (internal link in Redwood Console)
- Slack channels: #enterprise-support, #oncall-sre
- GitHub repo: github.com/redwood-inference/enterprise-onboarding (internal)

B. Quick CLI snippets
- Validate API key:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
- Example generation call:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1","input":"Translate to French: Hello"}'

C. Ownership and maintenance
- Primary owner: Aisha Patel (Customer Success) - maintain this playbook and onboarding artifact bundle.
- Technical reviewers: SE team (Marco Ruiz), Support lead (Daniel Kim).
- Review cadence: annual review and after any enterprise incident affecting >1 customer.

Document history:
- 2025-11-10 - created by Aisha Patel
- 2026-02-15 - last updated (added Known Issues section and updated SLA times)

End of playbook.
